title: Finance Business Partner
company: Three Bridges Recruitment LTD - Agency - Permanent
description:

- Salary of £47,000 - £51,000 pro rata
- Initial 6-month contract with the possibility of extension

As Finance Business Partner, you will:

- Interpret business reporting needs & develop financial reports, data analysis & operational KPIs
- Provide financial insight to help ensure finance processes & outputs are understood, followed & responsive to the needs of the organisation
- Develop & maintain costing & other financial models
- Work with all colleagues to understand requirements & communicate information clearly
- Identify opportunities to improve financial systems, reporting & processes
- Manage competing priorities & deliver accurate work within tight deadlines

You

As Finance Business Partner, you will:
- Bring strong technical & analytical skills with a proactive, collaborative approach
- Have experience developed in a similar or equivalent finance role
- Have strong budgeting, forecasting & management accounting experience
- Have experience of systems optimisation & improving financial processes
- Have practical experience applying accounting regulations
- Be proficient in specialist financial systems & Microsoft applications, particularly Excel
- Have experience working within a large or complex organisation
- Be able to interpret complex financial information & communicate it in a clearly
- Be highly motivated, adaptable & comfortable managing competing deadlines
- Have strong interpersonal skills, with confidence to work with all stakeholders
- Bring demonstrable negotiation & conflict resolution skills
- Ideally have experience within the not-for-profit sector, although this is not essential
- Be available to start as soon as possible & within four weeks

At Three Bridges Recruitment, two of our values are "striving for brilliance" & "relatability". We want every applicant to receive an excellent experience & ensure that this opportunity is the right fit for you. Should this role be of interest, please apply with your most up-to-date CV or contact us for a confidential discussion.

title: Group Payroll Administrator
description:
Group Payroll Administrator

Location: Falkirk area
Contract: Full-time, Permanent
Working Arrangement: Fully office-based

The Opportunity

We are working with a growing, multi-entity business operating across the UK that is looking to appoint an experienced Group Payroll Administrator on a full-time, permanent basis.

This role will suit a payroll professional with experience managing payroll across multiple businesses or legal entities, each with its own processes, pay structures and operational requirements.

You will be responsible for ensuring accurate and timely payroll processing across a collection of entities, managing varying payroll requirements and ensuring employees are paid correctly and on time.

Key Responsibilities
- Manage end-to-end payroll processing across multiple group entities, adapting to each entity's specific requirements and procedures.
- Calculate and process overtime, commission, bonuses, allowances, travel expenses and other variable pay elements.
- Maintain accurate employee records, processing starters, leavers, salary changes, contractual amendments and changes to working hours.
- Process PAYE, National Insurance, pension contributions, statutory payments and other payroll deductions accurately.
- Complete payroll checks and reconciliations, investigate discrepancies and resolve issues ahead of pay dates.
- Coordinate different payroll deadlines, ensuring all inputs and approvals are received and processed on time.
- Maintain accurate payroll records and ensure compliance with relevant legislation and reporting requirements.
- Liaise with employees, managers and finance colleagues to resolve payroll queries and improve processes where possible.

About You

You will ideally have:
- Proven experience in payroll administration or processing, with demonstrable experience managing payroll across multiple entities or businesses.
- An understanding of the differences in payroll processes, pay structures and employee terms across separate entities.
- Experience processing variable pay, including overtime, commission, bonuses, allowances and expenses.
- A strong working knowledge of PAYE, National Insurance, pensions and statutory payments.
- Excellent numerical skills, strong attention to detail and a methodical approach to payroll checks and reconciliations.
- The ability to manage competing deadlines, work independently and take ownership of the full payroll process.
- Strong communication skills and a proactive, organised approach to resolving payroll queries.

If you have the payroll experience and attention to detail required to manage different payroll arrangements within a growing group, we would welcome your application.
